tweets.text:
Two skills that matter for vibe coding

Why I'm effective:

1. Know basic programming
Vibe coded Notifier with zero React/TypeScript experience. Understanding how code works kept it functional. Hired dev later to fix issues but foundation worked.

2. Build iteratively
Started to-do list with simplest version. Worked in one shot. Added complexity gradually: checkboxes, recurring tasks, editing.

Start simple, layer complexity.

Hard truth: Need some code understanding. Vibe coding without programming basics = editing novels without grammar.

tweets.text:
If you want to learn Vibe Coding fast (and for free), do this:

→ Dive into Next.js docs, cover FE (pages, components), BE (API routes), DB (Prisma/Supabase), and try 2-3 real code examples from each section  

→ Build 3 mini-projects: a weather dashboard, a notes app, and a simple chat interface—ship each one to GitHub  

→ Clone a real app (simplified): try Twitter, Notion, or Linktree—focus on auth, feed, and profile features  

→ Add AI-powered features: integrate GPT-4 API for smart search, or build a chatbot into your cloned project  

→ Polish with Tailwind, add mobile responsiveness, deploy on Vercel, and share your project on X + LinkedIn  

Do this 2-4 hours/day for 5-6 weeks  
Document your journey—post updates every week, ask for feedback, and connect with other devs  

By week 6, you’ll have 3+ projects, a real-world clone, and AI features in your portfolio 
 
You’ll stand out—most beginners never ship or share, but you’ll have proof of work and momentum
